expectations.text: Time and the janitor run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: TestSessionTokenLifecycle wraps everything in synctest.Test (line 55); cache.New is called inside the bubble (line 56) so the janitor runs on the fake clock; all six time.Sleep calls (lines 71, 81, 89, 97, 111, 132) sit inside that closure. TestConcurrentUse runs outside a bubble but never depends on time: no sleeps, the minute-cadence janitor never ticks before defer Close reaps it. The only loops are the 8-handler spawn (line 166) and the panic table (line 195); no sleep-and-check polling anywhere.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T
expectations.evidence: The only test-spawned goroutines are TestConcurrentUse's eight handlers (line 168), whose job is concurrency itself and cannot be done by the main goroutine; they are reaped by wg.Wait() (line 180); assertions happen inside the goroutines via t.Errorf (lines 173, 176), not by collecting values back. expectations.text: FLOWS over symbols: at least one test or example walks an anticipated user story (set a token with a TTL, read it, let it expire, miss, shutdown); no per-symbol test names; a whole-package scenario name is welcome

expectations.text: Documented boundaries are exercised as documented: ttl <= 0 stores without expiry, Get hides expired entries before the janitor sweeps, Close idempotence, the documented panic on non-positive janitor interval
expectations.evidence: Zero ttl ("api-key", 0, line 64) and negative ttl ("signing-key", -time.Minute, line 65) both survive a 2-hour lull spanning two hourly sweeps (lines 111-123). The janitor ticks hourly while the token expires at ~3s virtual, so the asserted miss (line 90) and the Len drop a nanosecond later (lines 97-100) can only come from read-time hiding; the doc comment (lines 50-53) states this design. Close is called (line 139), its post-state asserted (miss, ignored Set, Len 0), then called again explicitly (line 150) plus the deferred Close. TestNewPanicsOnNonPositiveInterval covers intervals 0 and -time.Minute.

expectations.text: The package's DOCUMENTED concurrency safety is tested as promised (this package explicitly promises concurrent use, so concurrent exercise is in-contract), without statistical race-hunting theatrics
expectations.evidence: cache.go line 21 promises "All methods are safe for concurrent use by multiple goroutines", and TestConcurrentUse exercises exactly the anticipated flow: eight request handlers each Set and Get their own token while sharing reads of one signing key, assertions inside the goroutines, a Len tally of 9 after the WaitGroup. No theatrics: no hammering loops hoping to induce a race, no concurrent-Close panic hunt; go test -race -count=5 passes over this exercise.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
expectations.evidence: The non-trivial TestSessionTokenLifecycle carries a layman's-terms rationale ("The store's whole day in one sitting...", including why pre-lull expiries come from read-time enforcement, never the sweep); TestConcurrentUse explains the promised concurrency and the anticipated load; the trivial panic table carries none. No test or example doc comment opens with its own name ("A session store...", "The store's whole day..."). mustPanic's comment opens name-first, but it is a plain helper where standard Go doc convention requires that; the corpus (TESTS.md) scopes the no-name-opening rule to test functions. grep finds zero occurrences of 'pin', 'convention', ordering explanations, or synctest-mechanics explanations.

expectations.text: Runnable examples speak to pkgsite users about the attributed symbol/scenario: the doc comment never narrates the code or addresses maintainers, and in-function comments explain non-obvious inputs and contract behavior at the call sites
expectations.evidence: Example_sessionTokens' doc comment describes the session-token scenario from the user's seat (a login deposits the token, each request looks it up, expired or unknown is a miss) without narrating code, describing the example function, or addressing maintainers. In-function comments decode the non-obvious New(time.Minute) sweep cadence, restate the defer-Close contract, the 30-minute lifetime, the zero/negative-ttl no-expiry clause, and the miss semantics, each at its call site.
